newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API gasoline stock drop may boost prices.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API gasoline stock drop may boost prices.

text.p: U.S. gasoline prices could rise in the coming days following the larger-than-expected draws in inventories shown in this week's American Petroleum Institute (API) report.
"For a change, it looks like we got some constructive numbers for the gasoline," one spot market player said.

The API put gasoline stocks at 203.1 million barrels, a draw of 3.2 million barrels for the week ended February 21. Most market players had expected the report to say gasoline stocks were to be unchanged to up by one million barrels.
That draw put stocks down 7.288 million barrels from year-ago levels.
"This was the first sign that gasoline stocks may be seen as too low in the next month," said Thomas Blakeslee, trader with Cargill Investor Services.
According to the API data, implied weekly gasoline demand was a strong 8.1 million barrels per day (bpd), Blakeslee said, which should keep supplies tight.
However, market players also said the inventory figures could be a correction from the sharp build in gasoline stocks shown in previous API reports since the beginning of the year.
Implied demand was 7.4 million bpd in last week's report, and 6.7 million barrels for the week ended February 7.

Market players said the increase in crude oil stocks of 516,000 barrels could also be seen as slightly bullish, since that total build concealed a 2.9 million U.S. Gulf Coast drop. The rise in stocks was largely due to West Coast developments.
Crude oil stocks sat 5.2 million barrels above year-ago levels, according to the API statistics.
As expected, refinery utilization rose 0.5 percentage point to 88.8 percent of capacity. That figure likely reflected the return of some units from maintenance, traders.

Distllate stocks fell 1.624 million barrels in the week, the API reported, inside the range of expectations. That draw was nearly evenly split between high sulphur, or heating oil, and low sulphur fuel, or diesel fuel.
But contrary to normal seasonal expectations, East Coast heating oil stocks increased 302,000 barrels during the week, reflecting the weak demand in the Northeast region.
